 1:34 am, November 14, 2026 No. 2 Oklahoma State overpowers No. 3 Nebraska 27-6 in Stillwater
 Under head coach David Taylor, the No. 2 Oklahoma State Cowboys have become of the most exciting, flashy, and funky programs in the country. This team was all of that and more against No. 3 Nebraska on Friday night in front of a sold-out crowd in Gallagher-Iba Arena, dominating the Cornhuskers 27-6. 
 Rocklin Zinkin kickstarted the team’s momentum with his 2-1 tie-breaker win over 2025 NCAA champion Vincent Robinson. Filling in for teammate and 2025 NCAA finalist Troy Spratley, the freshman Cowboy Zinkin looked right at home and proved that he’s ready to compete on this stage and at this level. His win highlights the dangerous depth of this program. 
 ROCKLIN ZINKIN https://t.co/mol8dY0fkC
— OSU Cowboy Wrestling (@CowboyWrestling) November 14, 2026 
 Following Zinkin, 2026 NCAA champion Jax Forrest did Jax Forrest things, rolling to a 21-6 win over No. 8 two-time NCAA All-American Jacob Van Dee. He’s looking every bit like a title favorite here in his second year with Oklahoma State. 
 Bonus points kept rolling for the Cowboys at 141 pounds as true freshman Jayden Raney notched a major decision over Lincoln Sledzianowski, 10-2. While he was one of just two Cowboys to notch bonus, including Forrest, his fight in this match and his push for points still served as a theme for Oklahoma State up and down the lineup. 
 Former national champions No. 2 Sergio Vega and No. 1 Landon Robideau picked up gritty wins themselves over No. 5 Anthony Echemendia and No. 3 Antrell Taylor at 149 and 157 pounds, respectively, by matching scores of 4-2. No. 3 Casey Swiderski followed with a statement win over three-time All-American Meyer Shapiro 4-2. These three matches — and the grit that those Cowboys showed through the final seconds of their matches to earn the win — embodied the team’s attitude up and down the lineup. These guys came to score. 
 ALL-AMERICAN ATHLETES: These were the 80 guys who finished on the podium last year 
 Despite dropping a nail-bitter at 174 pounds to No. 2 Christopher Minto, the Cowboys reset and responded at 184 pounds with a surging 9-4 win from No. 11 freshman Mikey White over No. 16 Lucas Cochran after a series of insurance takedowns in the third period. NCAA finalist Cody Merrill added to the team's total with an overtime takedown win over No. 5 two-time All-American Camden McDanel. 
 Nebraska picked up the win at heavyweight from No. 14 Cade Ziola 4-1 against Oklahoma State's Dreshaun Ross, but that win wasn't enough to overcome the gap the Cowboys had put between themselves the No. 3 Cornhuskers. 
 Oklahoma State made magic on Friday night. The Cowboys will have No. 14 Arizona State next week, but, tonight, they've shown they deserve the national respect of being one of the best teams in the country.

 share with Facebook copy link 1:05 am, November 13, 2026 Weight-by-weight preview of No. 2 Oklahoma State vs. No. 3 Nebraska
 125 pounds: No. 7 Troy Spratley OR Rocklin Zinkin vs. No. 4 Vincent Robinson 
 If the highest ranked starter for the Oklahoma State Cowboys and the Nebraska Cornhuskers took the mat on Friday and each wrestler only earned a decision, the Cowboys would win the dual 21-9. But duals hardly ever break that way, and given the unpredictability of wrestler results at the start of the season, every match will count. That dynamic makes this 125-pound match even more intriguing. Nebraska transfer junior Vincent Robinson will be favored against either Oklahoma State's No. 7 Troy Spratley or freshman star  Rocklin Zinkin, but, on paper, Spratley poses the better challenge. He faced Robinson in the 2025 NCAA finals and dropped the match 2-1 in overtime, but he also does have a win over the champ 8-5 at NCAAs last year. Though Spratley is 1-4 against Robinson, he's felt the poise and control of the Husker and knows what to expect. 
 Zinkin, on the other hand, is more unproven but could potentially throw chaos at Robinson in a way that puts him in a position for an upset. He got the nod last weekend against Drexel because of an injury that Spratley is fighting, but Zinkin proved he's capable of being a similar kind of Sparkplug for the Cowboys. He's 5-0 on the year with 100% bonus but no ranked wins, so his ceiling is still unclear. If he starts against Robinson at the weight where the Cowboys are, on paper, not favored regardless, fans will get a much better idea of his potential. If Spratley gets the start, expect this one to bring the intensity immediately and go into overtime.  
 133 pounds: No. 1 Jax Forrest vs. No. 8 Jacob Van Dee 
 Jax Forrest back in Gallagher-Iba Arena again means one thing: it's time for Funkytown. The 2026 Oklahoma State national champion picked up his sophomore year right where he left off last year, teching or pinning his last five opponents and ending all of his matches within the first two periods.
 THE ATMOSPHERE IN STILLWATER 😮‍💨 #NCAAWrestling x 🎥 @OSUAthletics https://t.co/J4DZFmBXjP
— NCAA Men's Wrestling (@NCAAWrestling) January 11, 2026 
 Forrest will have his first top-10 opponent of the year too in Nebraska two-time All-American Jacob Van Dee, and while Van Dee will be expected to push him more than his other competition this year, Forrest will still be looking for bonus points. Van Dee also lost his opening match of the year against Luke Willochell of Wyoming, meaning he's going against a red hot Forrest without momentum. Van Dee's strategy in his match will be to trying to slow down the Cowboy and avoid getting caught in the funk. 
 141 pounds: No. 15 Jayden Raney OR Tagen Jamison vs. Lincoln Sledzianowski OR No. 30 Jake Hockaday  
 The biggest storyline at 141 pounds is all about Oklahoma State's Jayden Raney. The blue-chip recruit from Kentucky came to Stillwater with a bright spotlight after winning gold at the U17 world championships in 2024 and qualifying for the senior world team in Greco in 2025. Now Raney's won the starting spot, at least for the time being, for the Cowboys after topping his teammate and NCAA qualifier Tagen Jamison 6-5 at the Cowboy Invite. He's also teched or pinned his Gardner-Webb opponents at the Invite to claim the 141 pound title and then teched Anthony DePaul of Drexel in his debut dual. If Nebraska sends out Jake Hockaday, Raney could see his first ranked opponent of the year, but, regardless of whether Hockaday or Lincoln Sledzianowski take the mat, look for Raney to show why he's ready to fill the shoes left behind by last year's NCAA champion Sergio Vega. 
 Tagen Jamison is also listed as a starter for Oklahoma State, and he's a formidable foe himself. A graduate student, Jamison is 45-18 in his Cowboy career and finished as high as the Round of 12 in 2025. He'd be favored against Hockaday or Sledzianowski as well. 
 149 pounds: No. 2 Sergio Vega vs. No. 5 Anthony Echemendia 
 This is the bout of the night. Oklahoma State's 2026 NCAA champion Sergio Vega has never been taken down in college and is known for his strong, steady defense. His opponent, two-time All-American Anthony Echemendia of Nebraska, is famous for the same. Both athletes are also moving up from 141 pounds last year and looking to make their mark on a new weight — this will be their first big challenge.
 Vega is 2-0 against Echemendia, but both matches were close, with the Cowboy winning the first, 4-2, at the dual and then squeezing out a 2-1 tiebreaker victory at Big 12s. A full-feed Vega vs. a full-feed Echemendia bodes well for seeing more points on the board and more action. This is a stacked weight too, so every win (and loss) will matter on an athlete's record heading into the postseason. Can Echemendia pull off the upset and deliver the Cowboy the first loss of his college career? The hometown crowd gives Vega an edge, but Echemendia is on the short list of athletes to watch who have the potential to challenge the champ. 
 Oklahoma State also has Jayden's brother, Jordyn, listed as a probable starter option at 149 pounds. While Echemendia would be favored over Raney, that would be a match worth watching, given Raney's pedigree as a high school wrestler, including his six Kentucky state titles, and his age group world championship experience. 
 157 pounds: No. 1 Landon Robideau vs. No. 3 Antrell Taylor 
 As if 149 pounds wasn't exciting enough, the projected match at 157 pounds features last year's two national finalists in Landon Robideau of Oklahoma State and Antrell Taylor of Nebraska. Robideau earned the last win 4-2, but Taylor did beat Robideau in last year's dual 3-2. This one is truly a coin-flip, but Nebraska will likely need the points to push the Cowboys for the team win. 
 Robideau is 4-0 on the year so far with three techs and a pin, and he looks big and strong this year as he chases a second title. Taylor is also undefeated though, having picked up a win by major against Antonio Avila of Wyoming 17-4. Taylor, who won NCAAs in 2025, is savvy and experienced, and he's someone who has proven he can beat the best. He gets another shot to do so again on Friday night. 
 165 pounds: No. 3 Casey Swiderksi vs. Meyer Shapiro  
 It's three-time All-American Meyer Shapiro vs. two-time All-American Casey Swiderski in the Transfer Bowl. Swiderski earned his starting spot for the Cowboys by beating teammate and NCAA qualifier LaDarion Lockett 4-3 in tie-breakers and teammate Kody Rutledge 4-1 in sudden victory at the Cowboy Invite, and he expanded his resume with a tech fall against Drexel. Now the former Iowa State starter who has found his place, his voice and his brand at Oklahoma State will take on former Cornell middleweight Meyer Shapiro who unexpectedly stepped in as a starter for the Huskers after announcing his intention to redshirt earlier this summer. 
 Shapiro wrestled down at 157 pounds for the Big Red last year and finished seventh, while Swiderski powered his way through the 149-pound bracket to finish eighth. Friday they meet at 165 pounds, and while Swiderski is favored on paper because Shapiro hasn't had ranked wins at the weight yet, this is a bout Nebraska could win to keep the dual competitive. A healthy, strong, funky, bulked-up Shapiro is dangerous against a scrappy force like Swiderski. Buckle up for this one. Emotions will run high in Stillwater when these two take the mat. 
 174 pounds: No. 12 Alex Facundo OR Lorenzo Norman vs. No. 2 Christopher Minto  
 If Shapiro can pick up momentum for the Huskers, Christopher Minto is the one Nebraska will want to pick up the mantle and keep the energy rolling. The two-time All-American and 2026 NCAA finalist comes into the year ranked No. 2 behind Penn State's Mitchell Mesenbrink, and he looked solid in his debut last weekend where he won 10-4 over No. 33 Riley Davis. Now he'll have one of two Cowboy options in No. 12 Alex Facundo or Lorenzo Norman.

 Facundo finished in the Round of 16 last year for Oklahoma State while Norman ended his year last year 1-2 at NCAAs for the Stanford Cardinal. Facundo topped the transfer veteran in their wrestle-off at the Cowboy Invite 7-5 and now has another shot against Minto after beating him 2-1 at the National Dual Invitational. Minto avenged the loss in the Oklahoma State-Nebraska dual 4-1, and Nebraska will need him to come up with the W again. While Minto will be favored because of his improvement and his accolades, Facundo has shown that he can't be overlooked. 
 184 pounds: No. 11 Mikey White vs. No. 18 Lucas Cochran OR Ethan DeLeon
 After the intensity of much of the middleweights, the 184-pound match in this dual will bring more intrigue, as Cowboy fans get another look at freshman Mikey White — who topped All-American transfer Bennett Berge at the Cowboy Invitational — and Nebraska fans learn where Penn State transfer Lucas Cochran or senior Ethan DeLeon stacks up in a high-stakes contest. Cochran went 4-0 at the Dakota Wesleyan Open, but teammate Ethan DeLeon earned the start against Drexel. DeLeon lost his bout to All-American Eddie Neitenbach, setting up a potential for Cochran to be the guy this week. White has never wrestled either of these guys in college yet, considering he's only competed on this stage for less than a week, but his performance against Cochran or DeLeon will be a useful measuring stick before the Cowboys gear up for Arizona State next week. 
 197 pounds: No. 2 Cody Merrill vs. No. 5 Camden McDanel  
 In another All-American vs. All-American matchup, Oklahoma State's Cody Merrill will be looking for his first top-ten win over the year after dropping his Cowboy Invite championship bout to three-time All-American Stephen Little of Little Rock following an injury. McDanel, meanwhile, likely has similar goals after losing his first match of the season last weekend to No. 4 Joey Novak of Wyoming 4-1. 
 Merrill is 2-0 against Nebraska's Camden McDanel, but the Husker has kept it close both times, dropping 2-1 in tie-breakers at the National Dual Invitational and 2-1 in the dual. The Cowboy also outplaced McDanel at NCAAs, finishing second to McDanel's 5th, and this is the kind of highly-ranked, elite matchup that fans could expect to see in a round like the semifinals of an NCAA bracket. If the dual starts at 125 pounds, pressure could be mounting for both teams when "Kung Fu Panda" starts playing and Merrill begins his walkout against an undefeated-on-the-season McDanel. 
 285 pounds: Dreshaun Ross vs. No. 14 Cade Ziola
 These two lineups are full of so many big names and known stars with loaded storylines, and heavyweight is no different. Oklahoma State freshman Dreshaun Ross earned the start for the Cowboys against Drexel in place of All-American teammate and No. 1-ranked Konner Doucet, a clear indication of his coaches' confidence in him and their belief in his ability to win a title as a rookie, much like his teammates Forrest, Vega and Robideau did last year. He'll face Nebraska's freshman big man Cade Ziola, the heavyweight the Huskers picked over former Nebraska All-American AJ Ferrari. These are two guys with true talent and the trust of their staffs. Ross brings a 4-0 record into the match, while Ziola is 1-0 — only one will leave Gallagher-Iba undefeated.
